resources.string: Selection Pad

Adds a floating pad of buttons that move the text selection precisely — one word or one character at a time — in apps where text can be selected by touch but not edited, such as a web page in a browser. It works by moving the selection handles the app already shows. It never reads, stores or sends the text: it uses only the position of the selection on screen.
Before you turn this on

Selection Pad uses Android's accessibility service so it can move the selection handles in other apps — that is the only way to reach text a keyboard cannot, such as a web page.

What it does with that access:

• Reads where the current selection starts and ends, as positions on screen.
• Sends taps and drags to move the selection handles, one per button press.

What it never does:

• It never reads the text itself, only positions and rectangles.
• It never stores the text or the selection. It keeps only its own settings, such as whether you closed the pad.
• It cannot send anything anywhere — the app has no internet access. It asks for no permission at all unless you turn on its notification, and that notification never leaves the phone.

Nothing happens until you enable the service yourself, and turning it off in Accessibility settings stops it completely.

What to do
Notification

Turn it on to show or close the pad from the notification list. Android asks you to allow notifications first; that is the only permission the app ever asks for, and the notification never leaves the phone.

Notifications are not allowed for Selection Pad, so the switch stays off. To allow them, open Settings → Apps → Selection Pad → Notifications. Tapping the switch asks again, or opens that page once Android stops asking.
The switch is on, but notifications are blocked for Selection Pad. Allow them in Settings → Apps → Selection Pad → Notifications, or tap the switch to turn it off.

Selection Pad was switched off. If you did not do that, your phone did: some phones turn off an accessibility service they consider unusual, without saying so. Turn it back on in Accessibility settings.
On this phone the setting that does it is “Block suspicious app activities”. Search for it in Settings and allow Selection Pad there first, or it may be switched off again.
Open Accessibility settings
I switched it off myself

Selection Pad is switched on in Accessibility settings, but Android is not running it, so the pad, the tile and the notification cannot work, and the app cannot start it itself. Turn Selection Pad off and on again in Accessibility settings, or restart the phone. If Selection Pad has no switch there, restart the phone.

Your phone\'s battery saver is allowed to stop Selection Pad. When it does, the service restarts on its own a little later, and anything the pad was doing is lost. To stop that, set Selection Pad to “Don\'t optimize” (or “Unrestricted”) in the list below. Some phones also have a switch of their own, such as “Allow background activity”.
